subject: maths
title: Year 2 Fractions
seo_title: Year 2 Fractions Worksheets: Halves, Thirds and Quarters of Shapes, Objects and Numbers
standard_text: Recognise, find, name and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity; write simple fractions for example, 1/2 of 6 = 3 and recognise the equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 fractions worksheets for the National Curriculum: equal parts, halves, thirds and quarters of shapes, 2/4 = 1/2, fractions of a set of objects, fractions of numbers and lengths, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A fraction needs equal parts. 2 equal parts are halves, 3 are thirds and 4 are quarters.
key_sub: To find 1/4 of 8, share 8 into 4 equal groups: each group has 2. Two quarters are the same as one half.
body_html:
Equal parts

A fraction is a part of a whole. The parts must be equal (the same size).

Equal partsEach part isWe write
2one half12
3one third13
4one quarter14

The bottom number tells you how many equal parts. The top number tells you how many parts you have.

Two quarters and three quarters

Two quarters are the same as one half: 24 = 12.

Fractions of a set and a number

To find 14 of a group, share it into 4 equal groups. Count one group.

Example

What is 13 of 9?

Share 9 into 3 equal groups: 3, 3 and 3. One group is 3.

Answer: 3

Example

What is 34 of 12?

Share 12 into 4 equal groups of 3. Take 3 groups: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

Answer: 9

Example

What is 12 of 10 cm?

Share 10 cm into 2 equal parts: 5 cm and 5 cm.

Answer: 5 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling 2 unequal parts “halves”Halves must be equal
Saying 13 of 9 is 66 is two groups. One group is 3
Saying 34 of 12 is 33 is only one quarter. Take 3 groups: 9
Thinking 14 is bigger than 13 because 4 is biggerMore parts means smaller parts
Counting the parts that are not shadedThe top number counts the shaded parts

faq.q: What fractions do Year 2 children learn?
faq.a: Year 2 children learn halves, thirds and quarters: 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4. They find them of shapes, lengths, groups of objects and numbers, and learn that 2/4 is the same as 1/2.

faq.q: How do you find 1/3 of a number?
faq.a: Share the number into 3 equal groups and count one group. For 1/3 of 12, make 3 groups of 4, so the answer is 4.
Cut two same-size shapes into 2 parts and into 4 parts. Shade 1 half and 2 quarters: the shading covers the same amount.
No. A whole cut into 4 equal parts has smaller parts than a whole cut into 3, so 1/3 is bigger than 1/4.

sets.title: Equal parts: halves, thirds and quarters

items.q: Which shape is cut into halves?
items.e: Halves are 2 equal parts. That is C. A has 2 parts, but they are not equal. B has 3 equal parts. D has 2 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is cut into quarters?
items.e: Quarters are 4 equal parts. That is B. A has 4 parts, but they are not equal. C has 3 equal parts. D has 2 equal parts.

items.q: Which shape is cut into thirds?
items.e: Thirds are 3 equal parts. That is A. B has 3 parts, but they are not equal. C has 4 equal parts. D has 2 parts that are not equal.

items.q: Which shape is not cut into equal parts?
items.e: Look for parts that are different sizes. That is D. A has 4 equal parts. B has 2 equal parts. C has 3 equal parts.

items.q: What fraction is shaded?
items.e: The shape has 2 equal parts. 1 part is shaded. So 12 is shaded (one half).

items.q: The shape has 4 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 4 equal parts are called quarters. Each part is one quarter: 14.

items.q: The shape has 2 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 2 equal parts are called halves. Each part is one half: 12.

items.q: The shape has 3 equal parts. What is each part called?
items.e: 3 equal parts are called thirds. Each part is one third: 13.

items.q: How many quarters make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into quarters has 4 equal parts. So 4 quarters make 1 whole: 44 = 1.

items.q: How many halves make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into halves has 2 equal parts. So 2 halves make 1 whole: 22 = 1.

items.q: How many thirds make 1 whole?
items.e: One whole cut into thirds has 3 equal parts. So 3 thirds make 1 whole: 33 = 1.

sets.title: Two quarters, three quarters and one half

items.q: What fraction is shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, so they are quarters. 2 parts are shaded. So 24 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction is shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts, so they are quarters. 3 parts are shaded. So 34 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction is not shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 3 are shaded, so 1 is not shaded. The answer is 14.

items.q: What fraction is not shaded?
items.e: There are 4 equal parts. 1 is shaded, so 3 are not shaded. The answer is 34.

items.q: Which shape has 34 shaded?
items.e: 34 needs 4 equal parts with 3 shaded. That is D. A shows 14. B shows 24. C has 4 parts, but they are not equal.

items.q: Which shape has 24 shaded?
items.e: 24 needs 4 equal parts with 2 shaded. That is B. A shows 34. C has 3 parts, not 4. D shows 14.

items.e: Count the shaded quarters in the bottom bar: 2. They cover the same as 12. So 12 = 24.

items.q: Which fraction is the same as 12?
items.e: Half of 4 quarters is 2 quarters. So 12 = 24.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Look at the shaded parts.
items.e: The shading stops at the same place. The bottom bar has more parts, but they are smaller. 12 = 24.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Look at the shaded parts.
items.e: The top bar is shaded further. 34 is more than 12 (which is 24).

items.q: The bars are the same size. Which is bigger?
items.e: Look at the bars: one third is longer than one quarter. Cutting into more parts makes smaller parts. So 13 is bigger than 14.

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Which is bigger: 12 of a cake or 14 of a cake?
items.e: Cut a cake into 2 and the pieces are big. Cut it into 4 and the pieces are smaller. So 12 is bigger.

items.q:
Count in quarters.
14, 24, 34, ?
items.e: The next one is 44. That is all 4 quarters, which is 1 whole.

items.q: How many quarters are in 34?
items.e: 34 means 3 quarters. The top number tells you how many parts.

items.q: Which two fractions are both right for the shaded part?
c: 14 and 12
22 and 12

24 and 12
items.e: 2 of the 4 equal parts are shaded: 24. That is half of the square too, so 24 = 12.

items.q: Ava says 14 is bigger than 13, because 4 is bigger than 3. Is she right?
c: No, 13 is bigger
items.e: Cutting into 4 parts makes smaller parts than cutting into 3. So 13 is bigger than 14.

sets.title: Fractions of a set of objects

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 4 counters. 1 is red. So 14 of the counters are red.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 3 counters. 1 is red. So 13 of the counters are red.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 4 counters. 2 are red. So 24 of the counters are red.

items.q: What fraction of the counters are red?
items.e: There are 4 counters. 3 are red. So 34 of the counters are red.

items.q: There are 6 counters in 2 equal groups. What is 12 of 6?
items.e: Share 6 into 2 equal groups: 6 ÷ 2 = 3. One group is 12.

items.q: There are 10 counters in 2 equal groups. What is 12 of 10?
items.e: Share 10 into 2 equal groups: 10 ÷ 2 = 5. One group is 12.

items.q: There are 8 counters in 4 equal groups. What is 14 of 8?
items.e: Share 8 into 4 equal groups: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. One group is 14.

items.q: There are 9 counters in 3 equal groups. What is 13 of 9?
items.e: Share 9 into 3 equal groups: 9 ÷ 3 = 3. One group is 13.

items.q: There are 6 counters in 3 equal groups. What is 13 of 6?
items.e: Share 6 into 3 equal groups: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. One group is 13.

items.q: There are 12 counters in 4 equal groups. What is 14 of 12?
items.e: Share 12 into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. One group is 14.

items.q: There are 14 counters in 2 equal groups. What is 12 of 14?
items.e: Share 14 into 2 equal groups: 14 ÷ 2 = 7. One group is 12.

items.q: There are 12 counters in 3 equal groups. What is 13 of 12?
items.e: Share 12 into 3 equal groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. One group is 13.

items.q: There are 8 counters in 4 equal groups. What is 34 of 8?
items.e: First find 14: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. You need 3 groups, not 1: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

items.q: There are 12 counters in 4 equal groups. What is 34 of 12?
items.e: First find 14: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. You need 3 groups, not 1: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

items.q: There are 8 counters in 4 equal groups. What is 24 of 8?
items.e: 14 of 8 is 2. Take 2 groups: 2 + 2 = 4. (24 is the same as 12, and half of 8 is 4.)

items.q: What is 12 of these counters?
items.e: There are 12 counters. Share 12 into 2 equal groups: 12 ÷ 2 = 6. One group is 12.

items.q: What is 14 of these counters?
items.e: There are 12 counters. Share 12 into 4 equal groups: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. One group is 14.

items.q: What is 13 of these counters?
items.e: There are 6 counters. Share 6 into 3 equal groups: 6 ÷ 3 = 2. One group is 13.

items.q: What is 34 of these counters?
items.e: There are 4 counters. First find 14: 4 ÷ 4 = 1. You need 3 groups, not 1: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

items.q: What is 12 of these counters?
items.e: There are 8 counters. Share 8 into 2 equal groups: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. One group is 12.

items.q: The ribbon is 10 cm long. It is cut into 2 equal parts. How long is 12 of the ribbon?
items.e: Share 10 cm into 2 equal parts: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. One part is 12.

items.q: The ribbon is 12 cm long. It is cut into 4 equal parts. How long is 14 of the ribbon?
items.e: Share 12 cm into 4 equal parts: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cm. One part is 14.

items.q: The ribbon is 12 cm long. It is cut into 3 equal parts. How long is 13 of the ribbon?
items.e: Share 12 cm into 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 cm. One part is 13.

items.q: The ribbon is 20 cm long. It is cut into 4 equal parts. How long is 14 of the ribbon?
items.e: Share 20 cm into 4 equal parts: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. One part is 14.

items.q: The ribbon is 8 cm long. It is cut into 4 equal parts. How long is 34 of the ribbon?
items.e: First find 14: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. You need 3 parts, not 1: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 cm.

items.q: The ribbon is 16 cm long. It is cut into 2 equal parts. How long is 12 of the ribbon?
items.e: Share 16 cm into 2 equal parts: 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm. One part is 12.

items.q: What is 12 of 20?
items.e: Share 20 into 2 equal groups: 20 ÷ 2 = 10. One group is 12.

items.q: What is 12 of 30?
items.e: Share 30 into 2 equal groups: 30 ÷ 2 = 15. One group is 12.

items.q: What is 13 of 15?
items.e: Share 15 into 3 equal groups: 15 ÷ 3 = 5. One group is 13.

items.q: What is 14 of 20?
items.e: Share 20 into 4 equal groups: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. One group is 14.

items.q: What is 12 of 50?
items.e: Share 50 into 2 equal groups: 50 ÷ 2 = 25. One group is 12.

items.q: What is 13 of 30?
items.e: Share 30 into 3 equal groups: 30 ÷ 3 = 10. One group is 13.

items.q: What is 14 of 40?
items.e: Share 40 into 4 equal groups: 40 ÷ 4 = 10. One group is 14.

items.q: What is 34 of 20?
items.e: First find 14: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. You need 3 groups, not 1: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15.

items.q: What is 24 of 12?
items.e: 14 of 12 is 3. Take 2 groups: 3 + 3 = 6. (24 is the same as 12, and half of 12 is 6.)

items.q: What is 34 of 16?
items.e: First find 14: 16 ÷ 4 = 4. You need 3 groups, not 1: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
items.e: Half of 6: share 6 into 2 equal groups. Each group has 3, so 12 of 6 = 3. (13 of 6 is 2, and 14 of 8 is 2.)

items.q: Which is more: 13 of 12 or 14 of 12?
items.e: 13 of 12 is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. 14 of 12 is 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 4 is more than 3.

items.q: What is 24 of 10?
items.e: 24 is the same as 12. Half of 10 is 5.

items.q: 12 of ? = 8
items.e: 8 is one half, so the whole is 2 halves: 8 + 8 = 16. Check: half of 16 is 8.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Mohammed eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza does he eat?
items.e: There are 4 equal slices, so each slice is a quarter. Mohammed eats 1 slice: 14.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. Leo eats 1 slice. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: 4 − 1 = 3 slices are left out of 4 equal slices. That is 34.

items.q: There are 30 children in a Year 2 class. Half of them have school dinners. How many children have school dinners?
items.e: Share 30 into 2 equal groups: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 children. One group is 12.

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Share 60 into 4 equal parts: 15 + 15 + 15 + 15 = 60. So a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: An hour has 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30: 30 + 30 = 60.

items.q: Noah has 12 biscuits. He eats 13 of them. How many biscuits does he eat?
items.e: Share 12 into 3 equal groups: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 biscuits. One group is 13.

items.q: Harry has 8 pencils. 34 of them are red. How many red pencils are there?
items.e: First find 14: 8 ÷ 4 = 2. You need 3 groups, not 1: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 pencils.

items.q: Isla has 20p. She spends half of it. How much does she spend?
items.e: Half of 20p: share 20p into 2 equal parts. 10p + 10p = 20p, so the answer is 10p.

items.q: Arjun has 50p. He gives half of it to his brother. How much does he give?
items.e: Half of 50p: 25p + 25p = 50p. So the answer is 25p.

items.q: 4 friends share 16 sweets equally. Each friend gets 14 of the sweets. How many sweets does each friend get?
items.e: Share 16 into 4 equal groups: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 sweets. One group is 14.

items.q: Ava has a ribbon 20 cm long. She cuts it in half. How long is each piece?
items.e: Share 20 cm into 2 equal parts: 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm. One part is 12.

items.q: A box has 12 eggs. 34 of the eggs are brown. How many eggs are brown?
items.e: First find 14: 12 ÷ 4 = 3. You need 3 groups, not 1: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 eggs.

items.q: Two cakes are the same size. Freya eats 13 of one cake. Kai eats 14 of the other cake. Who eats more?
items.e: A cake cut into 3 has bigger pieces than a cake cut into 4. 13 is bigger than 14, so Freya eats more.

items.q: Two sandwiches are the same size. Zara eats 12 of one. Aisha eats 24 of the other. Who eats more?
items.e: 24 = 12. Aisha has more pieces, but they are smaller. They eat the same amount.

items.q: Grace cuts a sandwich into 2 pieces. One piece is big and one is small. She says each piece is a half. Is she right?
c: No, each piece is a quarter
No, the pieces are not equal
items.e: Halves must be 2 equal parts. One piece is bigger, so they are not halves.

items.q: Evie has 20 apples. She gives away 14 of them. How many apples does she give away?
items.e: Share 20 into 4 equal groups: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 apples. One group is 14.

items.q: Jack has 20 grapes. He eats 14 of them. How many grapes are left?
items.e: 14 of 20 is 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Jack eats 5 grapes. 20 − 5 = 15 grapes are left (that is 34).

items.q: There are 10 children in the playground. Half of them are girls. How many are boys?
items.e: Half of 10 is 5, so 5 are girls. The other half are boys: 10 − 5 = 5 boys.

items.q: Half of George’s beads are blue. He has 9 blue beads. How many beads does he have altogether?
items.e: 9 beads are one half. The whole is 2 halves: 9 + 9 = 18 beads. Check: half of 18 is 9.

items.q: Ethan has 9 stickers. He gives 13 of them to Lily. How many stickers does Lily get?
items.e: Share 9 into 3 equal groups: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 stickers. One group is 13.
